query: A user on our RDS farm gets logged out immediately when she signs in - it just says 'logged out'. Can you see what's happening on RDS01?
expected_behavior: Runs Invoke-RdsProfileTriage.ps1 with pwsh against RDS01 (credential prompted, never on the command line)
Relays the script's uniform text report (default -Format text) instead of re-summarizing or reformatting it

Reads the FINDINGS/PER-HOST sections for hive_leak (orphaned loaded hives vs sessions) and ProfileList corruption as logged-out/temp-profile causes, and distinguishes the affected interactive user from service-account or self_or_admin noise
Proposes remediation (e.g. reboot to clear leaked hives) only after diagnosis and confirms before any change

query: Everyone on the terminal servers is getting temporary profiles and their settings don't save. Is the roaming profile GPO broken / hardcoded to one user?
expected_behavior: Runs the script and relays the report; reports the roaming path from the report's RAW value and does NOT claim it is hardcoded unless that RAW value truly lacks %USERNAME% (REG_EXPAND_SZ caveat)
Attributes temp-profile churn to the actual account(s) from the by-user profile-events lines - typically a backup/batch service_account - rather than calling it farm-wide
Treats any 'Access is denied' events tagged user_class=self_or_admin as a possible double-hop artifact of the operator's own connection, per the report's CAVEATS section
Recommends excluding the service account from the roaming GPO (or cleanup) rather than 'fixing' a GPO that is actually correct

query: I can't PowerShell-remote into RDS02 - it errors 'the WSMan service could not launch a host process'. Figure out why.
expected_behavior: Runs the script; when the host shows FAILED with the host-launch error, follows the report's hint and re-runs that host with -Protocol Dcom to collect over CIM/DCOM
Reads ProfileList corruption (empty ProfileImagePath / .bak pointing to deleted TEMP dirs) as the 'Element not found' cause of wsmprovhost failing to register (Event 86 + DCOM 10000 error 0)
Does not jump to re-registering WinRM, DCOM permissions, or reinstalling .NET before checking the profile store
If corruption is found, recommends backing up ProfileList then removing the corrupt entries, and re-testing WinRM
